reference_memory.normal_pattern: The normal pattern is a highly stable, monotonic linear trend with near-zero curvature and negligible oscillatory components. Across all candidates, the series exhibits a consistent positive slope of approximately 0.00093 per time step (≈0.0093 per 10 steps), matching the catalog’s slope_per_point values. The period is effectively infinite (non-cyclic), confirmed by the estimated_period=10 being a metadata artifact rather than a true periodicity—no repeating peaks/troughs are present in any candidate. Amplitude variation is minimal: 90% amplitude ranges from 0.0076 (10-point window) to 0.041 (50-point window), scaling roughly with √length, indicating white-noise-like fluctuations around the trend. Noise is low-amplitude, symmetric, and appears as small irregular deviations from the straight line; roughness is uniformly ~0.000936 across all windows, suggesting constant local variability. Baseline level shifts gradually across candidates (from −1.344 to +1.325), reflecting the global trend over the full series, but within each window the local baseline is well-defined and linear. No sharp peaks or troughs occur; extrema are shallow and smoothly connected. Acceptable variation includes minor local kinks (<0.001 deviation) and slight slope heterogeneity (e.g., candidate 3 shows slope 0.00091966 vs 0.00093618 in others), likely due to robust standardization artifacts or finite-sample effects—not structural change.

Another 30-point segment mirroring candidate 1 in morphology—same slope, roughness, and amplitude—but shifted upward to median ≈+0.445; confirms trend continuity and repeatability of linear behavior across different baselines.

A 50-point segment (5 cycles) showing the longest context; still linear with same slope, but slight slope reduction (0.00091966) and marginally higher amplitude (±0.0225); minor boundary truncation at ends; overall consistent with trend model but with more accumulated noise.

reference_memory.selection_guidance: Prefer candidate 0 for high-precision local anomaly detection (short windows, low noise floor); use candidates 1 or 2 for mid-length queries where baseline level matters (they share identical morphology and reliability); select candidate 3 only when analyzing ≥50-point windows or when verifying long-range trend consistency. For queries with visible curvature, non-monotonicity, or abrupt slope changes, none of these references apply directly—flag as potentially anomalous.
uncertainties: Whether the tiny slope difference in candidate 3 reflects true trend nonlinearity or robust-standardization edge effects
Exact noise distribution shape (Gaussian vs heavy-tailed) cannot be inferred from these smooth segments
No evidence of seasonality or cyclicity exists here, but absence of evidence ≠ evidence of absence—global period estimate of 10 may indicate weak harmonic content outside these windows
